predecessors.name: Ming dynasty
predecessors.text: the Đại Ngu lands of the Hồ, held by the Ming as Jiaozhi from 1407 and recovered by Lê Lợi

successors.name: Trịnh lords
successors.text: Đàng Ngoài, the Lê court's north under the Trịnh lords

successors.name: Nguyễn lords
successors.text: Đàng Trong, the Lê south under the Nguyễn lords

ledger.x: 29 April 1428: Lê Lợi is enthroned and founds the Lê dynasty.
28 November 1470: Lê Thánh Tông sails against Champa.
Fall 1479: Lê Thánh Tông invades Lan Xang.
November 1484: 'By November 1484, Thanh Tong and his forces had withdrawn back to Dai Viet'; no land was kept.
15 June 1527: Mạc Đăng Dung usurps the throne.
1533: the Revival Lê holds the provinces south of the Red River.
1571: the Nguyễn south is drawn as a separate state.
1571: the Lê land passes to the Trịnh and Nguyễn lords in Cliopatria's rows.

wars.name: Lam Sơn uprising
wars.outcome: Lê Lợi's rebellion ('began on the day after Tết in February 1418'; Battle of Tốt Động-Chúc Động in October 1426) drove out the Ming, who withdrew by 1428; Lê Lợi was crowned on 29 April 1428.

wars.name: Champa-Đại Việt War (1471)
wars.outcome: Vijaya fell on 22 March 1471; northern Champa was annexed and the border moved to the Cù Mông Pass; the Cham court survived at Panduranga and two Cham rulers submitted as vassals.

wars.name: Lê invasion of Lan Xang
wars.outcome: 'In fall 1479, Thánh Tông led an army of 180,000 men' and 'Luang Phabang was captured and the Laotian ruler Chakkaphat was killed'; no Lê territory was added (the Lan Xang dossier carries the contest over Luang Prabang, 1479-1484).

wars.name: Lê-Mạc War
wars.outcome: The Revival Lê took the provinces south of the Red River; the Ming ruled in 1540 that the Mạc governed the north and the Lê the south; the Mạc lost territory to the Trịnh from 1541, Thăng Long fell in 1572 and was retaken in 1573, and in 1592 Trịnh Tùng…

certainty.note: The Ming frontier in the north is approximate; no treaty line is dated on the pages.

The Cù Mông Pass border with Champa (1471-1611) is a named pass but the page gives no treaty or survey; the Central Highlands and Lan Xang edges are claims; the Red River line of 1540 is the Ming's ruling.
